sourceUnits.zh: 慕容皝
sourceUnits.en: Murong Huang.
sourceUnits.literal: Murong Huang.

sourceUnits.zh: 慕容皝，字元真，廆第三子也。
sourceUnits.en: Murong Huang, whose courtesy name was Yuanzhen, was Murong Hui’s third son.
sourceUnits.literal: Murong Huang, courtesy name Yuanzhen, was the third son of Murong Hui.

sourceUnits.zh: 龍顏版齒，身長七尺八寸。
sourceUnits.en: He had an imperial bearing, unusually square teeth, and stood seven feet eight inches tall.
sourceUnits.literal: Dragon face and “plaque” teeth; body height seven chi eight cun.

sourceUnits.zh: 雄毅多權略，尚經學，善天文。
sourceUnits.en: He was bold, resourceful, devoted to the classics, and adept at reading the stars.
sourceUnits.literal: Heroic and resolute, abundant in stratagem; esteemed classical learning; skilled in astronomy.

sourceUnits.zh: 廆為遼東公，立為世子。
sourceUnits.en: When Murong Hui was named duke of Liaodong, Huang was made his heir.
sourceUnits.literal: When Hui became Duke of Liaodong, he was established as heir apparent.

sourceUnits.zh: 建武初，拜為冠軍將軍、左賢王，封望平侯，率眾征討，累有功。
sourceUnits.en: Early in the Jianwu era he was named general who champions the army and left worthy prince, created marquis of Wangping, and led troops on several successful expeditions.
sourceUnits.literal: At the beginning of Jianwu, appointed General Who Champions the Army, Left Worthy Prince, enfeoffed Marquis of Wangping; led host in campaigns; repeatedly had merit.

sourceUnits.zh: 太甯末，拜平北將軍，進封朝鮮公。
sourceUnits.en: Late in the Taining era he became general who pacifies the north and was promoted to duke of Chaoxian.
sourceUnits.literal: At the end of Taining, appointed General Who Pacifies the North; advanced enfeoffment to Duke of Chaoxian.

sourceUnits.zh: 廆卒，嗣位，以平北將軍行平州刺史，督攝部內。
sourceUnits.en: When Hui died he succeeded him, serving as general who pacifies the north and acting governor of Pingzhou with authority over the whole command.
sourceUnits.literal: When Hui died, he succeeded the position; as general who pacifies the north acted as governor of Ping Province, supervising and holding the interior of the command.

sourceUnits.zh: 尋而宇文乞得龜為其別部逸豆歸所逐，奔死於外，皝率騎討之，逸豆歸懼而請和，遂築榆陰、安晉二城而還。
sourceUnits.en: Soon afterward Yuwen Qidegui was driven out by Yidougui of his separate division and died in exile; Huang led cavalry against Yidougui, who took fright and sued for peace; Huang then built the two cities of Yuyin and Anjin and withdrew.
sourceUnits.literal: Soon Yuwen Qidegui was by his separate division Yidougui expelled, fled and died outside; Huang led cavalry to campaign against him; Yidougui feared and requested peace; thereupon built the two cities of Yuyin and Anjin and returned.

sourceUnits.zh: 初，皝庶兄建威翰驍武有雄才，素為皝所忌，母弟征虜仁、廣武昭並有寵於廆，皝亦不平之。
sourceUnits.en: Earlier, Huang's elder half-brother Murong Han, general who establishes might, was brave in arms and of heroic talent, and Huang had long resented him. Huang's younger full brothers Murong Ren, general who campaigns against the caitiffs, and Murong Zhao, general who extends martial power, were both favored by Hui, which also displeased Huang.
sourceUnits.literal: At first, Huang's elder brother by a concubine, Han, the general who establishes might, was brave in warfare and had heroic talent; Huang had long been jealous of him. His younger brothers by the same mother, Ren, the general who campaigns against the caitiffs, and Zhao, the general who extends martial power, both enjoyed Hui's favor; Huang was also displeased with them.

sourceUnits.zh: 及廆卒，並懼不自容。
sourceUnits.en: When Hui died they all feared for their lives.
sourceUnits.literal: When Hui died, all feared they could not preserve themselves.

sourceUnits.zh: 至此，翰出奔段遼，仁勸昭舉兵廢皝。
sourceUnits.en: Murong Han fled to Duan Liao, while Murong Ren urged Murong Zhao to revolt and depose Huang.
sourceUnits.literal: Reaching this point, Han fled out to Duan Liao; Ren urged Zhao to raise troops and depose Huang.

sourceUnits.zh: 皝殺昭，遣使按檢仁之虛實，遇仁於險瀆。
sourceUnits.en: Huang executed Zhao and sent envoys to probe whether Ren’s situation was genuine; they encountered Ren at Xiandu.
sourceUnits.literal: Huang killed Zhao, sent envoys to investigate the truth of Ren’s situation, met Ren at Xiandu.

sourceUnits.zh: 仁知事發，殺皝使，東歸平郭。
sourceUnits.en: Ren saw his plot exposed, killed the messenger, and fled east to Pingguo.
sourceUnits.literal: Ren knew the affair had broken; killed Huang’s envoy; went east to return to Pingguo.

sourceUnits.zh: 皝遣其弟建武幼、司馬佟壽等討之。
sourceUnits.en: Huang dispatched his younger brother Murong You, general who establishes martial power, Marshal Tong Shou, and others to campaign against Ren.
sourceUnits.literal: Huang sent his younger brother You, the general who establishes martial power, marshal Tong Shou, and others to campaign against him.

sourceUnits.zh: 仁盡眾距戰，幼等大敗，皆沒於仁。
sourceUnits.en: Ren threw his whole army into the fight and crushed You’s force, capturing every commander.
sourceUnits.literal: Ren exhausted the host to resist battle; You and the others were greatly defeated, all lost to Ren.

sourceUnits.zh: 襄平令王冰、將軍孫機以遼東叛於皝，東夷校尉封抽、護軍乙逸、遼東相韓矯、玄菟太守高詡等棄城奔還。
sourceUnits.en: Xiangping magistrate Wang Bing and general Sun Ji rebelled in Liaodong against Huang; Eastern Yi Colonel Feng Chou, Protector Yi Yi, Liaodong chancellor Han Jiao, Xuantu prefect Gao Xu, and others abandoned their cities and fled back.
sourceUnits.literal: Xiangping magistrate Wang Bing and general Sun Ji rebelled in Liaodong against Huang; Eastern Yi Colonel Feng Chou, protector Yi Yi, Liaodong chancellor Han Jiao, Xuantu prefect Gao Xu, and others abandoned cities and fled back.

sourceUnits.zh: 仁於是盡有遼左之地，自稱車騎將軍、平州刺史、遼東公。
sourceUnits.en: Ren then controlled all territory east of the Liao, proclaiming himself general of chariots and cavalry, governor of Pingzhou, and duke of Liaodong.
sourceUnits.literal: Ren thereupon wholly possessed the land left of the Liao, styled himself General of Chariots and Cavalry, governor of Ping Province, Duke of Liaodong.

sourceUnits.zh: 宇文歸、段遼及鮮卑諸部並為之援，
sourceUnits.en: Yuwen Gui, Duan Liao, and other Xianbei chiefs backed him.
sourceUnits.literal: Yuwen Gui, Duan Liao, and the various Xianbei divisions all became his aid.

sourceUnits.zh: 皝前軍帥慕容評敗季龍將石成等於遼西，斬其將呼延晃、張支，掠千餘戶以歸。
sourceUnits.en: Huang’s forward commander Murong Ping defeated Shi Hu’s generals Shi Cheng and others in Liaoxi, slew Huyan Huang and Zhang Zhi, and brought home more than a thousand households.
sourceUnits.literal: Huang’s forward commander Murong Ping defeated Jilong’s generals Shi Cheng and others in Liaoxi, beheaded their generals Huyan Huang and Zhang Zhi, plundered over a thousand households and returned.

sourceUnits.zh: 段遼謀叛，皝誅之。
sourceUnits.en: When Duan Liao plotted revolt, Huang put him to death.
sourceUnits.literal: Duan Liao plotted rebellion; Huang executed him.

sourceUnits.zh: 季龍又使石成入攻凡城，不克，進陷廣城。
sourceUnits.en: Shi Hu sent Shi Cheng against Fancheng without success but seized Guangcheng.
sourceUnits.literal: Jilong again sent Shi Cheng to attack Fancheng, could not overcome it, advanced and took Guangcheng.

sourceUnits.zh: 皝雖稱燕王，未有朝命，乃遣其長史劉祥獻捷京師，兼言權假之意，並請大舉討平中原。
sourceUnits.en: Though he called himself King of Yan, he still lacked a court mandate, so he sent his chief clerk Liu Xiang to report his victory at the capital, explain his provisional assumption of authority, and ask for a major campaign to pacify the Central Plain.
sourceUnits.literal: Although Huang styled himself King of Yan, there was yet no court mandate; he thereupon sent his chief clerk Liu Xiang to report his victory at the capital, also explaining his provisional assumption of authority and requesting a great campaign to pacify the Central Plain.

sourceUnits.zh: 又聞庾亮薨，弟冰、翼繼為將相，乃表曰：臣究觀前代昏明之主，若能親賢並建，則功致升平；
sourceUnits.en: When Murong Huang learned that Yu Liang had died and Yu Bing and Yu Yi held power, he submitted a memorial: I have studied wise and foolish rulers of past ages. When they favored the worthy and elevated them together, the realm rose to peace;
sourceUnits.literal: Moreover, when he learned that Yu Liang had died and Yu Bing and Yu Yi had succeeded as generals and ministers, he submitted a memorial, saying: Your servant has closely observed the muddled and clear rulers of former ages; if they could treat the worthy with intimacy and elevate them together, then merit reached peaceful ascendancy;

sourceUnits.zh: 若親黨后族，必有傾辱之禍。
sourceUnits.en: when they favored kin and the empress's clan, overthrow and humiliation were sure to follow.
sourceUnits.literal: If they favored kin and the empress's clan, disaster of overthrow and humiliation was sure to follow.

sourceUnits.zh: 是以周之申伯號稱賢舅，以其身籓於外，不握朝權。
sourceUnits.en: Shen Bo of Zhou was praised as a worthy maternal uncle because he held a frontier fief and did not grasp court power.
sourceUnits.literal: Therefore Shen Bo of Zhou was called the worthy maternal uncle, because he was enfeoffed outside as a frontier lord and did not hold court power.

sourceUnits.zh: 降及秦昭，足為令主，委信二舅，幾至亂國。
sourceUnits.en: Even King Zhao of Qin, a capable ruler, trusted his two maternal uncles and nearly ruined the state.
sourceUnits.literal: Descending to King Zhao of Qin, who was enough to be called a fine ruler, he entrusted his two maternal uncles and nearly brought the state to disorder.

sourceUnits.zh: 逮于漢武，推重田蚡，萬機之要，無不決之。
sourceUnits.en: Emperor Wu of Han elevated Tian Fen until every vital decision passed through him.
sourceUnits.literal: Reaching Emperor Wu of Han, who elevated Tian Fen, none of the myriad affairs' essentials went undecided by him.

sourceUnits.zh: 及蚡死後，切齒追恨。
sourceUnits.en: After Fen died, the emperor gnashed his teeth in bitter regret.
sourceUnits.literal: After Fen died, the emperor gnashed his teeth in later regret.

sourceUnits.zh: 成帝暗弱，不能自立，內惑豔妻，外恣五舅，卒令王莽坐取帝位。
sourceUnits.en: Emperor Cheng was weak and could not stand alone; beguiled within by a beautiful consort and indulging the five maternal uncles without, he finally let Wang Mang seize the throne without effort.
sourceUnits.literal: Emperor Cheng was dim and weak, unable to stand on his own; inwardly confused by a beautiful wife, outwardly indulging the five maternal uncles, he finally let Wang Mang take the imperial throne without effort.

sourceUnits.zh: 每覽斯事，孰不痛惋！
sourceUnits.en: Reading such cases, who does not feel pain and regret!
sourceUnits.literal: Each time one reads these affairs, who does not feel pain and regret!

sourceUnits.zh: 設使舅氏賢若穰侯、王鳳，則但聞有二臣，不聞有二主。
sourceUnits.en: If maternal uncles were worthy like the Marquis of Rang or Wang Feng, one would hear of two ministers, not two rulers.
sourceUnits.literal: Suppose the maternal uncles were worthy like the Marquis of Rang and Wang Feng, then one would only hear of two ministers, not two lords.

sourceUnits.zh: 若其不才，則有竇憲、梁冀之禍。
sourceUnits.en: If they lacked talent, disasters like those of Dou Xian and Liang Ji followed.
sourceUnits.literal: If they lacked talent, there were the disasters of Dou Xian and Liang Ji.

sourceUnits.zh: 凡此成敗，亦既然矣。
sourceUnits.en: The lesson of these successes and failures is already plain.
sourceUnits.literal: All these successes and failures are already thus clear.

sourceUnits.zh: 苟能易軌，可無覆墜。
sourceUnits.en: Change course in time and collapse can be avoided.
sourceUnits.literal: If one could change course, one could avoid overturn and collapse.

sourceUnits.zh: 陛下命世天挺，當隆晉道，而遭國多難，殷憂備嬰，追述往事，至今楚灼。
sourceUnits.en: Your Majesty is heaven-born to exalt Jin's Way, yet the state has met repeated calamity; grief presses on every side, and recalling the past still burns.
sourceUnits.literal: Your Majesty is heaven-born to the age, destined to exalt Jin's Way, yet has encountered many hardships of state; deep grief presses on every side; recalling past affairs, to this day one burns with anguish.

sourceUnits.zh: 跡其所由，實因故司空亮居元舅之尊，勢業之重，執政裁下，輕侮邊將，故令蘇峻、祖約不勝其忿，遂致敗國。
sourceUnits.en: The root cause was the late Minister of Works Yu Liang: as chief maternal uncle he wielded overwhelming power, judged subordinates harshly, and insulted frontier generals until Su Jun and Zu Yue, unable to bear their rage, ruined the state.
sourceUnits.literal: Tracing where it came from, it was truly because the late Minister of Works Yu Liang occupied the honor of chief maternal uncle and the weight of power and achievement, governed and judged subordinates, and lightly insulted frontier generals, so that Su Jun and Zu Yue could not contain their rage and thus brought disaster on the state.

sourceUnits.zh: 至今太后發憤，一旦升遐。
sourceUnits.en: And now the Empress Dowager, overcome with indignation, has suddenly passed away.
sourceUnits.literal: Until now the Empress Dowager gave vent to her indignation and in one morning ascended to distant heaven.

sourceUnits.zh: 若社稷不靈，人神無助，豺狼之心當可極邪！
sourceUnits.en: Had the altars not been numinous and men and spirits not aided us, would the hearts of wolves and jackals have been allowed to run their course!
sourceUnits.literal: If the altars were not numinous and men and spirits gave no aid, would the heart of wolves and jackals be allowed to reach its limit!

sourceUnits.zh: 前事不忘，後事之表，而中書監、左將軍冰等內執樞機，外擁上將，昆弟並列，人臣莫疇。
sourceUnits.en: Remembering past events provides a guide for the future. Yet Yu Bing, Director of the Secretariat and General of the Left, and his fellows control the central levers of government within and hold senior military commands outside; the brothers stand side by side in office, with no other ministers to match them.
sourceUnits.literal: Past events, if not forgotten, are a model for later affairs; yet Yu Bing, Director of the Secretariat and General of the Left, and his fellows grasp the pivot within and hold senior military commands outside; the brothers stand side by side, with no other minister to match them.

sourceUnits.zh: 陛下深敦渭陽，冰等自宜引領。
sourceUnits.en: Your Majesty deeply honors family ties; Bing and his fellows ought naturally to look up in expectation.
sourceUnits.literal: Your Majesty deeply honors the ties of Weiyang; Bing and the others ought themselves to stretch their necks in expectation.

sourceUnits.zh: 臣常謂世主若欲崇顯舅氏，何不封以籓國，豐其祿賜，限其勢利，使上無偏優，下無私論。
sourceUnits.en: I have often said: if a ruler wishes to honor maternal kin, enfeoff them in vassal states, enrich their stipends, and limit their power so that the throne shows no partial favor and the realm no private suspicion.
sourceUnits.literal: Your servant often says: if a ruler of the age wishes to honor the maternal clan, why not enfeoff them with vassal states, enrich their stipends and gifts, and limit their power and advantage, so that above there is no partial favor and below no private talk.

sourceUnits.zh: 如此，榮辱何從而生！
sourceUnits.en: Then whence would honor or disgrace arise!
sourceUnits.literal: Thus, from what would honor and disgrace arise!

sourceUnits.zh: 噂𠴲何辭而起！
sourceUnits.en: Whence would slander spring!
sourceUnits.literal: From what words would slander and calumny spring!

sourceUnits.zh: 往者惟亮一人，宿有名望，尚致世變，況今居之者素無聞焉！
sourceUnits.en: Formerly Yu Liang alone, though long renowned, still brought turmoil; how much more those who hold power today and were never heard of before!
sourceUnits.literal: Formerly there was only Yu Liang alone, long with a name of standing, yet still he brought change to the age; how much more those who hold the posts today, who from the first had no renown!

sourceUnits.zh: 且人情易惑，難以戶告，縱今陛下無私于彼，天下之人誰謂不私乎！
sourceUnits.en: Human feelings are easily swayed and cannot be told house to house; even if Your Majesty is impartial, who in the realm will believe it!
sourceUnits.literal: Moreover human feelings are easily confused and hard to tell door to door; even if Your Majesty today has no partiality toward them, who in the realm would say there is none!

sourceUnits.zh: 臣與冰等名位殊班，出處懸邈，又國之戚昵，理應降悅，以適事會。
sourceUnits.en: Bing and I differ in rank and are far apart in our positions; moreover, he and his brothers are close relatives of the imperial house. By rights I ought to defer and accommodate myself to the circumstances.
sourceUnits.literal: Your servant and Bing and the others differ in rank and status and are far apart in our situations; moreover, they are close kin of the imperial house. By rights I ought to defer and accommodate myself to the circumstances.

sourceUnits.zh: 臣獨矯抗此言者，上為陛下，退為冰計，疾苟容之臣，坐鑒得失。
sourceUnits.en: I speak against the tide alone: for Your Majesty above and for Bing's sake below, hating ministers who only flatter and judging gain and loss plainly.
sourceUnits.literal: Your servant alone presses this contrary speech: for Your Majesty above, for Bing's sake below; despising ministers who only accommodate; sitting in judgment of gain and loss.

sourceUnits.zh: 顛而不扶，焉用彼相！
sourceUnits.en: If one does not right what is overturned, of what use is that minister!
sourceUnits.literal: If one does not right what is overturned, what use is that minister!

sourceUnits.zh: 昔徐福陳霍氏之戒，宣帝不從，至令忠臣更為逆族，良由察之不審，防之無漸。
sourceUnits.en: Formerly Xu Fu warned against the Huo clan; Emperor Xuan did not heed him, and loyal ministers became a traitorous house because he did not examine carefully or guard against gradual encroachment.
sourceUnits.literal: Formerly Xu Fu set forth the warning of the Huo clan; Emperor Xuan did not follow it, so that even loyal ministers became a rebellious lineage, truly because investigation was not careful and precautions were not taken at the first signs.

sourceUnits.zh: 臣今所陳，可謂防漸矣。
sourceUnits.en: What I now set forth is prevention at the first sign.
sourceUnits.literal: What your servant now sets forth may be called prevention at the first sign.

sourceUnits.zh: 但恐陛下不明臣之忠，不用臣之計，事過之日，更處焦爛之後耳。
sourceUnits.en: I fear only that Your Majesty may not see my loyalty or use my plan, and that after disaster passes you will again stand amid the ashes.
sourceUnits.literal: Only fearing that Your Majesty may not understand your servant's loyalty and may not use your servant's plan; after the affair has passed, one will again be in the charred wreckage.

sourceUnits.zh: 昔王章、劉向每上封事，未嘗不指斥王氏，故令二子或死或刑。
sourceUnits.en: Formerly Wang Zhang and Liu Xiang denounced the Wang clan in every sealed memorial and ended dead or punished.
sourceUnits.literal: Formerly Wang Zhang and Liu Xiang, each time they submitted sealed memorials, never failed to denounce the Wang clan, so both men ended dead or under punishment.

sourceUnits.zh: 谷永、張禹依違不對，故容身苟免，取譏於世。
sourceUnits.en: Gu Yong and Zhang Yu equivocated and preserved themselves, winning only the age's ridicule.
sourceUnits.literal: Gu Yong and Zhang Yu equivocated and did not answer directly, so they preserved themselves and escaped, drawing ridicule from the age.

sourceUnits.zh: 臣被髮殊俗，位為上將，夙夜惟憂，罔知所報，惟當外殄寇仇，內盡忠規，陳力輸誠，以答國恩。
sourceUnits.en: I wear disheveled hair in a foreign land, hold supreme command, worry day and night how to repay the state, and can only destroy enemies abroad and offer loyal remonstrance within.
sourceUnits.literal: Your servant wears disheveled hair in a foreign land, holds the rank of supreme general, worries day and night and knows not how to repay, and can only destroy enemies abroad, exhaust loyal remonstrance within, exert strength and offer sincerity to answer the state's grace.

sourceUnits.zh: 臣若不言，誰當言者！
sourceUnits.en: If I do not speak, who will!
sourceUnits.literal: If your servant does not speak, who will speak!

sourceUnits.zh: 又與冰書曰：君以椒房之親，舅氏之昵，總據樞機，出內王命，兼擁列將州司之位，昆弟網羅，顯布畿甸。
sourceUnits.en: He also wrote to Yu Bing: By empress kinship and maternal closeness you hold the pivot, issue and receive royal commands, and with your brothers hold command and provincial posts, your network displayed across the capital region.
sourceUnits.literal: Again he wrote to Bing, saying: You, by the intimacy of the empress's chamber and closeness as maternal kin, hold the pivot in total, issue and receive royal commands, and together hold the posts of generals and provincial overseers; your brothers spread a net, displayed across the capital region.

sourceUnits.zh: 自秦、漢以來，隆赫之極，豈有若此者乎！
sourceUnits.en: Since Qin and Han, has splendor reached such a height!
sourceUnits.literal: Since Qin and Han, has there been such extreme splendor!

sourceUnits.zh: 以吾觀之，若功就事舉，必享申伯之名；
sourceUnits.en: In my view, if your work succeeds you will enjoy Shen Bo's fame;
sourceUnits.literal: In my view, if merit is achieved and affairs succeed, you will surely enjoy the name of Shen Bo;

sourceUnits.zh: 如或不立，將不免梁竇之跡矣。
sourceUnits.en: if not, you will not escape the fate of Liang Ji and Dou Xian.
sourceUnits.literal: If not, you will not escape the track of Liang Ji and Dou Xian.

sourceUnits.zh: 每睹史傳，未嘗不寵恣母族，使執權亂朝，先有殊世之榮，尋有負乘之累，所謂愛之適足以為害。
sourceUnits.en: Reading the histories, I see maternal relatives indulged and allowed to wield power and disorder the court: first they enjoy extraordinary glory, then suffer the consequences of holding positions beyond their station. This is what is meant by love proving sufficient to cause harm.
sourceUnits.literal: Whenever I read the histories, I see maternal relatives invariably pampered and indulged, allowed to hold power and disorder the court; first they enjoy glory surpassing their age, then incur the burden of riding when unfit; this is what is meant by love being sufficient to cause harm.

sourceUnits.zh: 吾常忿歷代之主，不盡防萌終寵之術，何不業以一土之封，令籓國相承，如周之齊、陳？
sourceUnits.en: I have often resented that successive rulers did not fully master the means of preventing incipient trouble while preserving favor to the end. Why not establish these relatives with a territorial fief and let their descendants inherit the vassal state, as with Qi and Chen under Zhou?
sourceUnits.literal: I often resent that rulers of successive ages did not fully use the art of preventing incipient trouble and preserving favor to the end; why not establish them with a territorial fief and let the vassal states be inherited in succession, as with Qi and Chen under Zhou?

sourceUnits.zh: 如此則永保南面之尊，復何黜辱之憂乎！
sourceUnits.en: Then they would forever preserve honor facing south, with no fear of dismissal or disgrace!
sourceUnits.literal: Then they would forever preserve the honor of facing south; what worry of dismissal and disgrace!

sourceUnits.zh: 竇武、何進好善虛己。
sourceUnits.en: Dou Wu and He Jin loved goodness and humbled themselves.
sourceUnits.literal: Dou Wu and He Jin loved goodness and emptied themselves.

sourceUnits.zh: 賢士歸心，雖為閹豎所危，天下嗟痛，猶有能履以不驕，圖國亡身故也。
sourceUnits.en: Worthy men rallied to them; although eunuchs brought them into peril, the realm lamented them because they could nonetheless conduct themselves without arrogance and gave their lives for the state.
sourceUnits.literal: Worthy men gave them their hearts; although they were endangered by eunuch minions, the realm lamented them, because they were still able to conduct themselves without arrogance and took thought for the state at the cost of their lives.

sourceUnits.zh: 方今四海有倒懸之急，中夏逋僭逆之寇，家有漉血之怨，人有復仇之憾，甯得安枕逍遙，雅談卒歲邪！
sourceUnits.en: Now the realm hangs inverted, rebels roam China, families bear blood-soaked grievances and men thirst for vengeance; how can one rest at ease and talk elegantly through the year!
sourceUnits.literal: Now the four seas have the urgency of the inverted hanging; within China flee usurping rebels; families bear blood-soaked grievances and men the regret of vengeance; how can one rest on pillows at ease, discoursing elegantly through the year!

sourceUnits.zh: 吾雖寡德，過蒙先帝列將之授，以數郡之人，尚欲併吞強虜，是以自頃迄今，交鋒接刃，一時務農，三時用武，而猶師徒不頓，倉有餘粟，敵人日畏，我境日廣，況乃王者之威，堂堂之勢，豈可同年而語哉！
sourceUnits.en: Though deficient in virtue, I undeservedly received appointment as one of the former emperor’s generals. With the people of only several commanderies, I still aspire to engulf powerful enemies. Thus, from recent times until now we have crossed weapons in battle, farming for one season and fighting for three; yet our troops are not exhausted, our granaries have surplus grain, our enemies fear us more each day, and our territory grows daily. How much greater, then, are imperial majesty and its imposing power—how could the two be compared!
sourceUnits.literal: Though deficient in virtue, I undeservedly received the former emperor's appointment among the generals; with the people of several commanderies I still wish to swallow powerful enemies; therefore from recent times until now, crossing weapons and meeting blades, one season for farming and three for war, yet the troops are not exhausted, the granaries have surplus grain, the enemy fears us more each day and our territory grows daily; how much greater, then, are imperial majesty and its imposing power—how could the two be compared!

sourceUnits.zh: 冰見表及書甚懼，以其絕遠，非所能制，遂與何充等奏聽皝稱燕王。
sourceUnits.en: On seeing the memorial and the letter, Yu Bing was greatly alarmed; because Huang was so far away and beyond his power to control, he joined He Chong and others in memorializing that Huang be allowed to style himself King of Yan.
sourceUnits.literal: Bing, seeing the memorial and letter, was greatly afraid; because Huang was extremely far away and beyond his power to control, he thereupon, with He Chong and the others, memorialized to permit Huang to style himself King of Yan.

sourceUnits.zh: 其年皝伐高句麗，王釗乞盟而還。
sourceUnits.en: That year he invaded Goguryeo; King Gao Zhao sued for peace and he withdrew.
sourceUnits.literal: That year Huang campaigned against Gaogouli; King Gao Zhao begged a covenant, and Huang returned.

sourceUnits.zh: 明年，釗遣其世子朝於皝。
sourceUnits.en: The next year Gao Zhao sent his heir to pay homage to Huang.
sourceUnits.literal: The next year, Zhao sent his heir apparent to court at Huang.

sourceUnits.zh: 初，段遼之敗也，建威翰奔于宇文歸，自以威名夙振，終不保全，乃陽狂恣酒，被髮歌呼。
sourceUnits.en: After Duan Liao’s fall Murong Han fled to Yuwen Gui, reckoned his fame would never let him live, and feigned madness—drinking, singing, and disheveled hair.
sourceUnits.literal: In the beginning, when Duan Liao was defeated, Jianwei Han fled to Yuwen Gui; himself thought his awe-inspiring name long had shaken others, in the end could not preserve whole; thereupon feigned madness, wantonly drank, let hair down and sang and shouted.

sourceUnits.zh: 歸信而不禁，故得周遊自任，至於山川形便，攻戰要路，莫不練之。
sourceUnits.en: Yuwen Gui trusted the act and left him free, so Han mapped every defile and road.
sourceUnits.literal: Gui believed and did not restrain; therefore was able to roam at will, reaching mountains and rivers’ forms and conveniences, attack and battle crucial roads—none not practiced.

sourceUnits.zh: 皝遣商人王車陰使察翰，翰見車無言，撫膺而已。
sourceUnits.en: Huang sent the trader Wang Che to spy; Murong Han met him in silence, only clutching his chest.
sourceUnits.literal: Huang sent merchant Wang Che secretly to observe Han; Han seeing Che spoke nothing, stroked his breast only.

sourceUnits.zh: 車還以白，皝曰：「翰欲來也。」
sourceUnits.en: Wang Che reported the sign; Huang said, “He wants to come home.”
sourceUnits.literal: Che returned and reported; Huang said: “Han wishes to come.”

sourceUnits.zh: 乃遣車遺翰弓矢，翰乃竊歸駿馬，攜其二子而還。
sourceUnits.en: He sent Wang Che with a bow and arrows; Murong Han stole horses and rode back with his two sons.
sourceUnits.literal: Thereupon sent Che to present Han bow and arrows; Han then stole fine horses, carried his two sons and returned.

sourceUnits.zh: 皝將圖石氏，從容謂諸將曰：「石季龍自以安樂諸城守防嚴重，城之南北必不設備，今若詭路出其不意，冀之北土盡可破也。」
sourceUnits.en: Planning against the Shi, he told his commanders, “Shi Hu trusts his garrisons at Anle and neglects the open country north and south of the wall—a sudden raid could overrun the whole Ji plain.”
sourceUnits.literal: Huang was about to plan the Shi clan; leisurely said to the generals: “Shi Jilong thinks the cities of Anle and the rest guard defense strict and heavy; surely north and south of the city he does not set equipment; now if by deceitful route go out where he does not expect, the whole north of Ji can be broken.”

sourceUnits.zh: 於是率騎二萬出蠮螉塞，長驅至於薊城，進渡武遂津，入于高陽，所過焚燒積聚，掠徙幽、冀三萬餘戶。
sourceUnits.en: He then led twenty thousand cavalry out through Yeweng Pass, drove straight to Ji city, advanced across Wusui Ford into Gaoyang, burning the stores wherever he passed, and carried off more than thirty thousand households from You and Ji.
sourceUnits.literal: Thereupon he led twenty thousand cavalry out through Yeweng Pass, drove straight to Ji city, advanced across Wusui Ford, and entered Gaoyang; wherever he passed he burned the stores, and he plundered and relocated more than thirty thousand households from You and Ji.
